meta.title: Coaxially Bioprinted Cell-Laden Tubular-Like Structure for Studying Glioma Angiogenesis.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: Coaxial printing made hollow alginate microfibres with glioma cells in the shell and endothelial cells in a collagen core, to study how glioma drives blood vessel formation.

formulations.name: 2% alginate shell (glioma) / collagen core (HUVEC)
formulations.composition_detail: Shell: 2% sodium alginate with U118 glioma cells; core: 1 mg/mL collagen with HUVECs
formulations.cell_type: U118 glioma cells + HUVEC endothelial cells
formulations.key_outcome: Shell/core fibres let glioma-endothelial interaction and vessel-like formation be studied in a tubular structure.

evidence.quote: U118-RFP cells were resuspended in 2% sodium alginate solution as shell stream with a concentration of 1 × 106/ml
to obtain a core stream with cell concentration of 1×105/ml and final collagen concentration of 1 mg/ml
The printing device is mainly consisted of a sheath/core nozzle, which composed of two concentric circles (inner diameters:0.577 mm, 1.469 mm, respectively).
